articles.title: Beautiful landscapes may briefly put the brakes on the brain’s movement system
articles.summary: Beauty has long been described as something that makes us pause and look. Neuroscientists in Italy tested that idea by recording brain activity while people viewed nature photos, and found signs that liked images dampened movement preparation.

articles.title: Early trauma may change how children’s cortisol responses relate to anxiety and behavior problems
articles.summary: Children who experience trauma early in life don’t all develop the same problems. A new study suggests their cortisol response to stress may help predict whether anxiety or acting out becomes more prominent as they grow.

articles.title: New study explores how money influences interpretations of the Bible
articles.summary: A large survey of Americans reveals that household income strongly shapes how religious individuals interpret the Bible’s teachings on charity, challenging the long-held idea that faith universally suppresses the desire for systemic economic change.

articles.title: Diets high in fat and sugar are linked to impulsiveness in people with borderline personality disorder
articles.summary: Adults with borderline personality disorder who ate more foods high in fat and sugar tended to be more impulsive and took more risks on a gambling task, though their diets were unrelated to overall symptom severity.

articles.title: A mirror trick that adds a sixth finger also changes what people think their hand can grab
articles.summary: With a mirror and some well-timed brushstrokes, researchers gave volunteers the sensation of a sixth finger. Afterward, people judged that their hand needed a wider opening to fit through and could grasp larger blocks.

articles.title: Intelligence and fertility: Do smarter people have fewer children? The strongest evidence suggests a smaller, more complicated link
articles.summary: People with higher intelligence scores tend to have slightly smaller families in American and British surveys. But when researchers wait until people finish having children and compare brothers from the same families, the link shrinks or even reverses.

Researchers found that brain signals associated with recognizing faces become more specialized as neurotypical children grow older, but show much less change in autistic children. articles.title: This mysterious mushroom makes people see hundreds of tiny humans
articles.summary: For nearly a century, people in distant parts of the world have reported a bizarre experience after eating certain wild mushrooms: seeing dozens or even hundreds of tiny, colorful humans moving through the real world. Now, scientists have identified a mushroom species, Lanmaoa asiatica, responsible for these extraordinary hallucinations in China and the Philippines.

articles.title: Mediterranean diet may boost tiny proteins that protect the heart and brain
articles.summary: Scientists have uncovered a surprising new clue to why the Mediterranean diet is so good for the heart, brain, and healthy aging. Researchers at USC found that older adults who closely followed the diet had higher levels of two tiny proteins, humanin and SHMOOSE, produced by the mitochondria, the energy-producing structures inside cells. These proteins have been linked to protection against heart disease…

articles.title: Breakthrough PTSD treatment achieves 68% remission rate in clinical trial
articles.summary: A newly FDA-cleared PTSD treatment uses personalized brain mapping and magnetic stimulation to target abnormal brain activity, with a clinical trial reporting a 52% reduction in symptoms and 68% remission. Researchers believe the technology could transform PTSD care and pave the way for more precise treatments for other mental health conditions.

articles.title: Scientists discover a hidden messaging system deep inside the brain
articles.summary: A tiny region deep within the brain has surprised scientists by revealing a remarkably sophisticated communication system. Previously thought to broadcast the same chemical signal throughout the brain, this region actually sends targeted messages that help control learning, attention, and behavior, according to new research in mice.

articles.title: Millions take fish oil for brain health. A two-year study found no benefit
articles.summary: A surprising two-year clinical trial found that fish oil supplements successfully delivered omega-3s to the brain but failed to improve memory or protect against Alzheimer's-related brain shrinkage. Researchers suspect that getting these nutrients through a healthy diet may offer benefits that supplements alone cannot provide.

articles.title: A simple daily fiber supplement reduced arthritis pain and improved strength
articles.summary: A new clinical trial suggests that a simple daily fiber supplement could significantly reduce knee osteoarthritis pain, improve muscle strength, and make the body less sensitive to pain. Researchers discovered that the benefits may be linked to changes in gut bacteria and the hormone GLP-1, revealing a promising new approach to arthritis relief.

articles.title: Low testosterone may make sugar far more harmful to your liver
articles.summary: Scientists have discovered that low testosterone and a high-fructose diet can work together to worsen fatty liver disease in mice. Unexpectedly, changes in gut bacteria appear to drive this harmful interaction, revealing a potential new target for preventing liver damage.

articles.title: Scientists discover a surprising clue to why some brains resist Alzheimer’s
articles.summary: Why do some people stay mentally sharp even when their brains show signs of Alzheimer’s disease? Scientists in the Netherlands may have uncovered an important clue hidden in a rare group of immature brain cells. Researchers discovered that these cells remain present even in people over 80, but their behavior differs dramatically between those who develop dementia and those who remain cognitively healthy.

articles.title: Just two drinks a day may be far riskier than you think
articles.summary: A major new study reveals that drinking just two alcoholic beverages a day is associated with a 1 in 25 lifetime risk of death from alcohol-related causes, challenging the idea that moderate drinking is harmless. Researchers also found no significant overall health benefits from alcohol, with risks rising as consumption increases.

articles.title: Low-dose aspirin linked to 70% lower dementia risk, but there's a catch
articles.summary: A common, inexpensive medication could hold an unexpected clue to preventing dementia. Researchers found that older adults with a specific genetic profile had a 70% lower relative risk of dementia when taking low-dose aspirin, even though previous studies found no overall protective effect. The discovery suggests that genetics could help explain why some people benefit while others do not.

articles.title: Popular cannabis sleep gummies may have a hidden dark side
articles.summary: A cannabis-derived ingredient commonly found in sleep gummies may be more habit-forming than previously thought, with new research showing that repeated exposure caused tolerance and withdrawal symptoms in mice. Scientists warn that CBN may carry risks similar to THC, although its long-term effects in humans remain largely unknown.
